Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwvm.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 13 s. 2023 MAR 13 2023 RENIER JN B. BORNAS Acting Head Corporate Legal Services Division Social Security System East Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City Dear Mr. Bornas: This refers to your letter dated November 3, 2022, requesting this Department's legal opinion on the legal rules/issuances governing dispute resolution on contracts executed between local government units and government-owned or controlled corporations. Per your letter, the Social Security System (SSS) has programs that involve partnerships with local government units (LGUs), namely: (1) the Kalta SSS-Collect program that employs workers under a job order or contract of service (subject workers). Under this program, the participating LGU shall collect and remit their subject workers' monthly SSS premium contributions to the SSS; and (2) the Contribution Subsidy Provider Program (CSPP), wherein an LGU can act as a Contribution Subsidy Provider that will subsidize the social security contributions of their subject workers, informal sections, or other identified members. During the SSS' finalization and/or enhancement of its contract provisions, an issue arose as to the applicable rule/s or rules that will govern the resolution of disputes, claims, or controversies involving the MOAs or lease contracts that may arise between the SSS and the LGUs. It is noted that the prevailing rule on dispute resolution between government agencies and instrumentalities and GOCCs is the "Uniform Rules on Dispute Resolution under Presidential Decree No. 242, as amended, for Government Agencies and Instrumentalities, and Government-Owned or Controlled Corporations" (Uniform Rules). Section 8.1 thereof provides that it "shall not apply to disputes involving the Congress, the Supreme Court, the Constitutional Commissions, and Local Government Units." Hence, the subject query. As aptly noted, the aforesaid Presidential Decree categorically excludes the local government units from its coverage. Such being the case, this level submits that local government units—anchored on the principle of local autonomy—have the leeway to stipulate the terms and conditions—including the provisions on dispute Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

resolution—regarding any potential disagreement, dispute, controversy, or claim vis-å-vis the contract that may be agreed upon by the other party, provided that such stipulations are not contrary to law, morals, good customs, public order, or public policy. Absent such stipulations, the New Civil Code of the Philippines, specifically the provision on partnerships and contracts, shall apply. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you.
